questions.question: 10 is the mean of a set of 7 observations and 5 is the mean of another set of 3 observations. The mean of the combined set is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mean of the first set of 7 observations = 10

Mean of the second set of 3 observations = 5

**Formula Used:**

Mean of the combined set = (Sum of all observations in the first set + Sum of all observations in the second set) / (Number of observations in the first set + Number of observations in the second set)

**Calculation:**

Sum of all observations in the first set = 10 × 7 = 70

Sum of all observations in the second set = 5 × 3 = 15

Total number of observations = 7 + 3 = 10

Mean of the combined set = (70 + 15) / 10

⇒ Mean of the combined set = 85 / 10

⇒ Mean of the combined set = 8.5

**The mean of the combined set is 8.5**

questions.question: If A + B = 45º, then (1 + tan A) (1 + tan B) = ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A + B = 45º

**Formula used:**

tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B) ÷ (1 - tan A tan B)

For A + B = 45º, tan(45º) = 1

**Calculation:**

1 = (tan A + tan B) ÷ (1 - tan A tan B)

⇒ 1 - tan A tan B = tan A + tan B

Now, expand (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B):

(1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 1 + tan A + tan B + tan A tan B

Substitute tan A + tan B = 1 - tan A tan B:

(1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 1 + (1 - tan A tan B) + tan A tan B

⇒ (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 1 + 1 = 2

**∴ (1 + tan A)(1 + tan B) = 2.**

⇒ 36 - 50 + 10

• There are **2 types** of Indian river systems.
 
• The Indian river systems are broadly classified into **Himalayan rivers** and **Peninsular rivers**.
 
• **Himalayan rivers** are perennial, originating from glaciers and snowfields in the Himalayas.
 
• **Peninsular rivers** are largely rain-fed and have seasonal flows.
 
• The classification is based on the origin, flow pattern, and the type of basin they form.

• The **Peninsular river system** includes rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery, which flow within the Indian subcontinent and have relatively smaller drainage basins.
 
• Rivers in India play a crucial role in **agriculture, hydropower generation, and transportation**.
 
• India has a rich tradition of river worship and reverence, with many rivers considered sacred in Hinduism and other religions.
 
• The management and conservation of river systems are critical for sustaining India's **ecosystems and livelihoods**.

questions.question: Raju is thrice as good as a workman as Vinod and together they can finish a task in 21 days. In how many days can Vinod alone complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Raju is thrice as good as Vinod.

Raju and Vinod together can finish the work in 21 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work Rate = Work / Time

Combined Work Rate = Sum of Individual Work Rates

**Calculation:**

Let the amount of work Vinod can do in one day be V.

Since Raju is thrice as good as Vinod, the amount of work Raju can do in one day is 3V.

Combined work rate of Raju and Vinod = V + 3V = 4V

Given that together they can finish the work in 21 days, so:

4V × 21 = 1 (whole work)

4V × 21 = 1

⇒ V = 1 / (4 × 21)

⇒ V = 1 / 84

Time taken by Vinod alone to complete the work:

⇒ Time = 1 / V

⇒ Time = 1 / (1 / 84)

⇒ Time = 84 days

**Vinod alone can complete the work in 84 days.**

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of distances covered: **A : B** = (60 − 12) : (60 + 12) = 48 : 72 = **2 : 3**.

Since time is constant, **Speed Ratio = Distance Ratio** = 2 : 3.

Difference in speed units = 3 − 2 = 1 unit.

Given speed difference = 4 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 4 km/h.

Speed of A = 2 units = 2 × 4 = 8 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Distance covered by **A** = 60 − 12 = 48 km.

Since both start at the same time and meet, the **time taken** is equal.

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ 48 / (v − 4) = 72 / v

⇒ 48v = 72(v − 4)

⇒ 2v = 3(v − 4)

⇒ 2v = 3v − 12

⇒ v = 12 km/h (Speed of B)

⇒ Speed of A = v − 4 = 12 − 4 = 8 km/h.

**∴ The correct answer is 8 km/h.**

questions.question: ₹200 was invested for 2 years on 10% compound interest per year. If the rate of interest had been 20%, then how much more would the investor have received as interest for the same period?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Rate of Interest** for 2 years at 10% = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 21%

Effective **Rate of Interest** for 2 years at 20% = 20 + 20 + (20 × 20)/100 = 44%

Difference in **Effective Percentage** = 44% − 21% = 23%

Additional Interest = 23% of **Principal** (₹200) = (23 ÷ 100) × 200 = ₹46

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹200

**Time (T)** = 2 years

**Initial Rate (R₁)** = 10% per annum

**New Rate (R₂)** = 20% per annum

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest (CI) = P[(1 + R/100)T − 1]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f6ca0caac85e6e7606faf0c9fe155d0037dabd2935fe98e79db0d502ee59360.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest at 10% (CI₁) = 200 × [(1 + 10/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI₁ = 200 × [(1.1)² − 1] = 200 × [1.21 − 1]

⇒ CI₁ = 200 × 0.21 = ₹42

⇒ Interest at 20% (CI₂) = 200 × [(1 + 20/100)² − 1]

⇒ CI₂ = 200 × [(1.2)² − 1] = 200 × [1.44 − 1]

⇒ CI₂ = 200 × 0.44 = ₹88

⇒ **Difference** in Interest = CI₂ − CI₁

⇒ Difference = 88 − 42 = ₹46

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Concept

Compound interest is calculated on the principal amount and also on the accumulated interest of previous periods.

Successive Percentage Formula

For a 2-year period, the effective rate is given by Rₑff = x + y + (xy/100), where x and y are the rates for each year.

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is P(R/100)².
